how.title: How we show numbers
how.intro: The observatory does not produce figures. It shows numbers published by named agencies, with a link to the original, the period measured and the kind of number it is. When a source cannot be shown honestly, we say so instead of showing a number.
how.dates.body: Each figure carries the period it measures, the date the source published it, and the time we received it. The time we received a figure says nothing about how recent the figure is.
how.stale: Old numbers are not shown as current
how.stale.body: Every indicator has a validity limit. Once the measured period is older than that, the card reads "No recent verified data available". The old value stays in the history with its dates. A failed update never shows as zero.
how.compare.body: A change is shown only between two values from the same source, with the same definition, coverage and type of number, for periods of equal length that do not overlap. Charts follow the same rule: points with different definitions are never joined by a line.
how.sources.body: We do not average figures or hide the gap. Each indicator names a primary source; other sources are listed next to it, each under its own name and link.
how.casualties.body: Deaths and injuries are separate cards and are never summed. Conflict-event data (ACLED) counts events and reported fatalities under ACLED's own method; it is not an official or complete toll. We never derive a death toll from headlines.
how.economic.body: A monetary figure appears only when a reliable report states what it measures, the currency, the reference prices or period, and the method. We never add up estimates from different reports into a "cost of the war".
how.corrections.body: Values are never overwritten. A correction is a new version that names what changed; the replaced value stays visible, struck through, in the history. Sensitive numbers are approved by a second person before they appear.
how.sections.body: A story's language, its publisher's country and the places it is about are stored separately. Sections follow the places a story is about, using declared country lists that editors can change:
how.ranking.body: Most relevant = {recency}% recency (halving every {half} hours) + {breadth}% breadth of coverage (how many publishers carry the story) + {reliability}% source reliability. Sources are not hidden for covering a story from a different angle.
how.translation.body: Stories appear in their original language, marked as such. Machine translation is not enabled; when it is, it will be labelled and will link back to the original.

gh.security: The token can write only to this repository and expires on the date you chose. It stays in this browser, and every change is recorded in the repository's history under your name.

gh.no_write: This token cannot write to the repository. Give it Contents: Read and write.
gh.how_it_works: Changes are saved to the repository and appear on the site after the next build (about 5–8 minutes).
gh.rebuild.no_permission: This token cannot start builds (Actions permission). Your saved changes start a build anyway.
